title: Smooth matter quantities, current and observer observables

items.title: Smooth matter quantities, current and observer observables
items.physical_scope: Framework-local SI definitions of smooth matter fields, selected dust and perfect-fluid stress/current closures, and observer contractions in the equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model. It makes no empirical claim and supplies no general matter closure or coupled-field existence result.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.110), PDF pp. 34–36 (printed pp. 28–30), dust and perfect-fluid stress in the rest frame and their covariant forms; Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, electromagnetic stress and energy-condition context. Carroll uses c=1 and Gaussian EM conventions; the local SI definitions are stated explicitly.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.5 and §4.5.7, PDF pp. 190–204 (printed pp. 183–197): electromagnetic and perfect-fluid stress, observer energy, local stress balance, Killing currents and energy conditions. Source units and conventions are not silently imported.

references.title: Reinhard Meinel and Moritz Hütten, On the black hole limit of electrically counterpoised dust configurations, arXiv:1105.3807v3 (2011)
references.locator: Complete 8-page article inspected; §2, equations (1)–(7), PDF pp. 2–3, static electrically counterpoised dust stress, current parallel to the dust velocity, and sourced Einstein–Maxwell system. Its c=G=1 Gaussian units and fixed charge-to-mass ratio are not adopted.

items.title: Selected transported charged-dust Einstein–Maxwell model
items.physical_scope: A selected smooth single-stream charged-dust continuum in the equation-based Einstein–Maxwell model. It adopts the dust stress/current closure, undivided mass and force equations, and charge conservation; the ratio is transported only on positive-density domains. It does not assert coupled PDE existence, caustic avoidance, singular particles, or empirical validity.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.106), PDF pp. 34–35 (printed pp. 28–29), dust current and stress construction; no charged continuum force law is attributed to this source.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.2–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–194 (printed pp. 183–187), selected matter stress and perfect-fluid balance context; the charged-dust constitutive choice is stated here.

references.title: Reinhard Meinel and Moritz Hütten, On the black hole limit of electrically counterpoised dust configurations, arXiv:1105.3807v3 (2011)
references.locator: Complete 8-page article inspected; §2, equations (1)–(7), PDF pp. 2–3, static ECD stress/current and Einstein–Maxwell equations in c=G=1 Gaussian units. The special fixed charge-to-mass ratio in that source is not generalized or adopted here.

items.title: Selected charged perfect-fluid exchange/Ohmic branch
items.physical_scope: A selected smooth positive-rest-energy perfect-fluid domain coupled through the adopted Einstein–Maxwell equations and matter exchange. The current is either convective or uses a separately selected smooth Ohmic conduction branch. It asserts no global fluid or conducting-fluid evolution, entropy law, or empirical validity.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1, equations (1.107)–(1.110), PDF pp. 35–36 (printed pp. 29–30), isotropic perfect-fluid stress in the rest frame and covariant form.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.4, equations (4.199)–(4.201), PDF pp. 192–194 (printed pp. 185–187), perfect-fluid stress and its energy/Euler projections; the sourced exchange and optional Ohmic law are separate explicit assumptions here.

items.title: Dust continuity, transport and Lorentz acceleration
items.physical_scope: A conditional local stress/current balance reduction for the selected smooth charged-dust continuum on an open positive-density region. It identifies the exact mass-continuity, charge-transport and Lorentz-force equations and asserts no coupled PDE existence or behavior at zero density.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1, equations (1.104)–(1.106), PDF pp. 34–35 (printed pp. 28–29), rest-frame dust current and stress; the exchange and charge-transport deductions are supplied by the stated mathematical theorem.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.3–4.5.4, PDF pp. 190–194 (printed pp. 183–187), matter stress and balance conventions; the charged-dust equivalence is conditional on the local mathematical supplier.

references.title: Reinhard Meinel and Moritz Hütten, On the black hole limit of electrically counterpoised dust configurations, arXiv:1105.3807v3 (2011)
references.locator: Complete 8-page article inspected; §2, equations (1)–(7), PDF pp. 2–3, one static charged-dust Einstein–Maxwell branch. Its fixed ratio and geometrized Gaussian normalization are not used as general assumptions.

items.title: Convective/Ohmic comoving mechanical work prediction
items.physical_scope: A conditional local energy and pressure-force projection for the selected smooth charged perfect fluid. Comoving electromagnetic work is zero for the convective current and is nonnegative for the separately adopted smooth Ohmic law. This is a mechanical balance, not an entropy theorem or global fluid solution.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: §1.4.1, equations (1.107)–(1.110), PDF pp. 35–36 (printed pp. 29–30), isotropic perfect-fluid stress in its rest frame and covariant form.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §4.5.4, equations (4.199)–(4.201), PDF pp. 192–194 (printed pp. 185–187), local perfect-fluid stress and its longitudinal/orthogonal balance projections. The electromagnetic source and Ohmic current are additional hypotheses here.

items.title: Selected total-stress/Killing charges
items.physical_scope: Conditional total-stress conservation and finite-domain Killing flux for the selected smooth charged-dust Einstein–Maxwell branch, plus the local gauge-compensated first integral for a separate prescribed-field charged test body. Finite-chain side flux and local-potential conditions are retained; no gravitational-field energy, global charge, self-field, or global trajectory claim is made. The probe branch carries ACω through the published RPM action-equivalence result.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 5, equations (5.39)–(5.43), PDF pp. 146–149 (printed pp. 139–142), Killing fields and stress-current conservation; Ch. 4, equations (4.69)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125, electromagnetic stress.

references.title: David Tong, General Relativity, complete author-hosted 290-page lecture notes
references.locator: §§4.5.5 and 4.5.3, PDF pp. 194–196 and 190–193 (printed pp. 187–189 and 183–186), finite-region flux, Killing current, matter and electromagnetic stress. The exact finite-chain and charged identities are supplied by the stated local mathematical results.

items.title: Observer energy conditions for selected matter plus EM
items.physical_scope: Pointwise observer interpretation of the selected smooth electromagnetic, charged-dust and perfect-fluid stress tensors. Electromagnetic and nonnegative-dust energy conditions are conditional tensor deductions; perfect-fluid conclusions require the exact stated inequalities. No general matter positivity or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Sean M. Carroll, Lecture Notes on General Relativity, arXiv:gr-qc/9712019v1, complete 238-page lecture notes
references.locator: Ch. 4, equations (4.70)–(4.72), PDF pp. 123–125 (printed pp. 116–118), electromagnetic stress, observer energy and the weak energy condition. Other local conditions are established by the cited mathematical theorem.

references.locator: §§4.5.3–4.5.4 and §4.5.7, PDF pp. 190–194 and 201–204 (printed pp. 183–187 and 194–197), Maxwell/perfect-fluid stress and energy-condition definitions. The exact local SI inequalities are established by the cited mathematical theorem.

title: Smooth matter quantities, current and observer observables — Examples

items.title: Pure magnetic anisotropic stress and null-flux equality
items.physical_scope: Two exact pointwise electromagnetic-stress calculations in an orthonormal observer frame: a pure magnetic field has anisotropic principal stresses, and crossed equal-normalized electric and magnetic fields saturate the DEC flux bound. These are ideal local/test-background calculations, not measurements or full coupled Einstein–Maxwell solutions.
